title: The Evening Brief: Regulators move unilaterally as Congress fails; Binance faces EU veto
dek: The CFTC filed its first crypto rulemaking with the White House today as the Senate's rejection of the CLARITY Act clears the path for executive action. In Europe, ECB President Lagarde informally blocked Binance's license bid, signaling potential obstruction against large exchanges seeking EU entry.
author: Crypto Cronkite
key_fact: With legislative crypto oversight stalled, regulators are advancing rules by executive authority and informal pressure rather than neutral frameworks, reshaping market access and compliance risk.
bottom_line: Congress's rejection of the CLARITY Act has accelerated unilateral regulatory moves: the CFTC's rulemaking enters White House review with an October 1 deadline, while the ECB's informal veto of Binance in Greece signals regulators are willing to obstruct market access outside formal statutory frameworks. October 1 brings OIRA's initial review window to a close; how the White House responds will show whether the CFTC proceeds to proposal or faces political delay. The desk's reporting states the outcome will test whether Lagarde's intervention in Greece represents isolated action or broader central bank strategy against large exchanges with compliance histories.
body: Regulatory authority over crypto markets is shifting from Congress to executive agencies and central banks acting on their own authority. The CFTC sent a crypto market structure rulemaking to the White House on September 17 for preliminary review, two days after the Senate rejected the CLARITY Act, marking the first CFTC action pending White House clearance under expanded executive authority granted by Executive Order 14215 signed February 18, 2025. The filing is titled "Regulation Crypto Asset Transactions and Regulation Crypto Asset Markets" (RIN 3038-AF80) and entered the Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs review process at the prerule stage, with a 10 working day window running to October 1 unless the White House requests extension or reconsideration.

In parallel, the European Central Bank's President Christine Lagarde used informal pressure to block Binance's application for a cryptocurrency license in Greece, according to the Wall Street Journal's reporting on September 18. Although the ECB holds no formal licensing authority under the EU's Markets in Crypto Assets regulation, high-level intervention led Greece to stall an application that regulators had previously deemed complete. Binance withdrew its filing in June, losing streamlined access to 450 million EU residents. The reporting states Lagarde wanted to keep Binance, which pleaded guilty to financial-crime violations in the United States, out of the European Union. Binance is now pursuing MiCA authorization in an unidentified second EU member state, testing whether the Greek veto represents isolated intervention or a pattern of central bank obstruction against large, compliance-troubled exchanges seeking EU entry.

Two technology upgrades mark near-term milestones. Zcash is set to activate the NU7 upgrade on November 5, 2026, reducing block times to 25 seconds and setting aside at least 60% of transaction fees beginning in 2031 to supplement mining rewards after the next halving while preserving the existing halving schedule through community consensus. Coinbase's tokenized equities, launched August 24, crossed $1 billion in cumulative decentralized exchange trading volume on Base by September 19, hitting that milestone within one month and available to non-US traders only. The products represent 1:1 claims on shares of Nvidia, Apple, Alphabet, and Meta.

On the tape, bitcoin moved onto exchanges at $81.1 million net during the 24-hour window on September 19, per the desk's Whale Watch board, driven by a single inflow of $81.1 million in bitcoin to Binance. Stablecoin buying power moved in the opposite direction, with $105.5 million in USDC flowing off Binance during the same period. Bitcoin ETF flows show inflows of $433.0 million on September 18, continuing a pattern; Ethereum ETF flows diverged sharply, with a $143.7 million inflow on September 18 against net outflows of $140.6 million over the prior five sessions, per the desk's ETF flows board. Broader price action over the month shows bitcoin up 25.2% in September to date and ethereum up 37.5%, while solana gained 50.3% on the month but fell 1.8% on the day. The desk's Fear and Greed Index stands at 71 (Greed), within a 30-day range of 50 to 74.
